title: Annual Large Bank Capital Requirements
summary: This Federal Reserve Board page explains the capital framework for large bank holding companies ($100B+ in assets), detailing how capital requirements are calculated using supervisory stress test results. The page provides reference links to annual capital requirement PDFs from 2020-2025 and explains the three components of CET1 capital ratio requirements: minimum requirement, stress capital buffer, and G-SIB surcharge.
key_points: Capital requirements apply to bank holding companies, covered savings and loan holding companies, and U.S. intermediate holding companies with $100 billion or more in total consolidated assets
Total CET1 capital ratio requirement comprises: minimum 4.5% CET1, stress capital buffer (SCB) of at least 2.5%, and G-SIB capital surcharge of at least 1.0%
SCB requirements are determined from supervisory stress test results and reflect 2022 stress test results per this page
Category IV firms were required to participate in the supervisory stress test this year, though they are generally exempt in odd years
Historical capital requirement PDFs available for 2020-2025 periods
why_it_matters: Understanding bank capital requirements is essential for market structure analysis because these requirements directly affect how large banks allocate capital across trading, market-making, and lending activities. Stricter requirements can constrain liquidity provision and increase funding costs, impacting overall market depth and resilience.
market_structure_context: This page provides foundational information on the regulatory capital framework governing large bank behavior in markets. The stress capital buffer requirement ties capital requirements to adverse economic scenarios, which influences how banks position themselves and manage risk in normal versus stressed market conditions.
